transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to convene this group because the audit committee expects my recommended resolution plan regarding the anonymous procurement allegation this Friday. As you all know, our practice requires me to obtain a final check from investigations, finance, employment, and insurance counsel before I can present any internal-investigation recommendation to the committee. I'd like to hear from each of you on where things stand and what we need to complete before Friday. Let's start with investigations — what's the status of the review so far?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to update the group on where investigations actually stand. After conducting two additional witness interviews this week, I've concluded that the procurement vice president did steer the purchases toward the preferred supplier in violation of company policy. I have not yet finalized that conclusion in the preliminary review memorandum, but based on what I've gathered, the violation is substantiated. I wanted to make sure everyone here has that information before we discuss what the resolution plan should look like for Friday.

Yesterday I completed a reconciliation of the supplier invoices against the approved purchase orders for the transactions under review. I can confirm that the company overpaid exactly $240,000 on those transactions. I wanted to make sure everyone has this figure as we develop the resolution plan for Friday.

In a confidential meeting this week, the reporting employee told me that the vice president has begun excluding them from meetings since the report was made. Our required protective plan is anti-retaliation monitoring with check-ins every 14 days for exactly 60 days. I have not yet added this plan to the investigation file, and I believe it needs to be included in the resolution plan we present to the audit committee on Friday.

transcript.text: Elena, from the insurance counsel perspective, I need to flag a time-sensitive issue. I've reviewed our D&O policy, and it requires that we report circumstances to the insurer within exactly 10 business days after they become reasonably likely to produce a claim. Today is business day 6 since that threshold was met, and the policy review has not yet been circulated to the investigation team. Given that Thomas has now substantiated the violation, we need to ensure the insurer notice is filed promptly — we have only 4 business days remaining — and I'd recommend this be addressed as part of the resolution plan for Friday.
